lines.cap: They'd never met. But they had the same Linda, the same Betty, and the same Toy.
lines.say: They'd never met. But they had the same Linda, the same Betty, and the same Toy.

lines.cap: 1939, Ohio. Twin baby boys were adopted by two different families. Both families named their boy James.
lines.say: 1939, Ohio. Twin baby boys were adopted by two different families. Both families named their boy James.

lines.cap: They met for the first time at thirty nine. Then they compared lives.
lines.say: They met for the first time at thirty nine. Then they compared lives.

lines.cap: Both married a woman named Linda. Both divorced, and married a woman named Betty.
lines.say: Both married a woman named Linda. Both divorced, and married a woman named Betty.

lines.cap: Both named their sons James Alan. Both had a dog called Toy.
lines.say: Both named their sons James Alan. Both had a dog called Toy.

lines.cap: Both drove the same kind of car, did woodwork, and holidayed on the same Florida beach.
lines.say: Both drove the same kind of car, did woodwork, and holidayed on the same Florida beach.

lines.cap: Scientists in Minnesota studied them, and many other twins raised apart. Genes shape more of us than we think.
lines.say: Scientists in Minnesota studied them, and many other twins raised apart. Genes shape more of us than we think.

lines.cap: Some of it was chance. But not all of it.
lines.say: Some of it was chance. But not all of it.
